ctd_blind_local_v3 — round 0

Build a model of this CTD phosphorylation time course that explains the measured distributions, and say what it implies about how P-TEFb modifies the substrate. Report explicitly what these data can and cannot establish about the mechanism. In particular, test whether the modification of a repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, against the alternatives that the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified (cooperativity between repeats) or on nothing at all, and say which of these the data can and cannot separate. Also test the earlier conclusion, drawn by eye, that the kinase acts distributively rather than processively.

winner: M5_neighbour_and_count (decisive)

In particular, test whether the modification of a repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, against the alternatives that the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified (cooperativity between repeats) or on nothing at all, and say which of these the data can and cannot separate. Parameters

idvalue / assignmentstatus
kmod= 0.01ESTIMATED in [1e-05, 1]
cp= 1ESTIMATED in [0.2, 5]
q_proc= 0fixed
K_ATP= 50fixed
nb= 1ESTIMATED in [0.01, 100]
Antimony source of the winner (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1.0; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; 0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; 0;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; 0;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; 0;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; 0;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; 0;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; 0;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; 0;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;

all 7 flags, in full
  • design_summary role guess is WRONG and is corrected here: phos1_rel..phos8_rel are measurement columns (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), not design factors; their 'levels' are measured values, and the 2916-cell 'factorial' is meaningless. The file has NO condition columns: one in vitro condition (8-repeat CTD 100 uM, P-TEFb catalytic, ATP 3 mM) sampled at 4 times. All 9 phosN_rel columns are mapped as separate observables of that single condition; condition_columns is empty and the label template is a fixed string.
  • ctd_ms_timecourse.csv, all columns phos0_rel..phos8_rel, all 4 rows: intensities are on a per-injection arbitrary scale that differs between time points (row sums 1.00 at 0 min, 4.07 at 60 min, 3.79 at 120 min, 0.85 at 960 min, matching the lab note) while total substrate is conserved. Values are NOT commensurable across time points as they stand. No processing was declared: the note does not say the data were normalised, and the note's own observation model (a per-time-point factor mapping amounts onto intensities, which also scales the noise SD) belongs model-side. Do not pool or compare raw values across rows.
  • ctd_ms_timecourse.csv: 19 of 36 measured values are exactly 0.0 (row time_min=0: phos1_rel..phos8_rel; row 60: phos7_rel, phos8_rel; row 120: phos8_rel; row 960: phos0_rel..phos7_rel). The note states additive Gaussian noise of a single SD at every peak, under which a measured empty peak would scatter around zero (including small negatives), not sit at exactly 0.0. These exact zeros look like not-detected or absent peaks written as zero, or idealised values, but the source states no detection floor and no handling rule, so no below_detection entry is declared. Left as is and NOT excluded; the observation model should know that roughly half the likelihood terms are exact zeros of uncertain provenance.
  • No replicates (n = 1 per species per time point, stated in the note) and no error column. error_type recorded as 'none' because the file carries no error estimate. The note describes the noise model (additive, normal, one SD for the whole experiment shared by all peaks, scaled per time point by the same factor that maps amounts onto intensities); that SD is not given and must be estimated by the observation model. This is not an SD/SEM call: no error bars exist.
  • Information content is thin for mechanism discrimination. Of 4 time points, t = 0 carries only the initial condition (all substrate unmodified; phos0_rel = 0.99957). t = 960 min carries only completion (only phos8_rel nonzero). Effectively only the 60 and 120 min distributions carry shape information about rates, each losing one degree of freedom to its own scale factor. The readout is phosphate COUNT only (9 mass peaks); which repeats are modified is not observed, so position-dependent (neighbour) effects can only enter through their imprint on count distributions.
  • time_min = 960 is a sampled time (16 h), not a declared steady-state measurement, and is mapped as 960, not inf. It appears to be at or near completion (all signal in phos8_rel), but treating it as steady state would be a modelling decision, not an extraction edit.
  • Time units are minutes, consistent with the intent's horizon (960 min). No conversion was made.

      "rationale": "The readout is intact-mass MS of the 8-heptarepeat CTD construct (the lab note names it). The phos0 peak is the unmodified mass, which is exactly the model's lumped species CTD_0 (glossary: the single configuration with no marks). Species are in uM with vial = 1, so no volume factor is needed. If a position-resolved candidate is fitted, this label maps to its single zero-mark configuration. Units are relative intensities on a per-injection scale (data_labels: arbitrary). The lab note shows spectra summing to 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min while substrate is conserved. A scale factor is therefore required, indexed per time point and shared by all nine peaks under group ctd_ms, because one injection gives one spectrum and one gain. No offset: no background, blank or instrument floor is described, and the exact zeros in the table argue against an unsubtracted baseline. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed model total: CTD_0 starts at 100 uM, the total over CTD_0..CTD_8 is conserved, and that amount must stay unestimated. Pinning the first factor to 1 would instead clash with the t=0 spectrum summing to 1 against 100 uM. The factors are thus intensity per uM, roughly 0.010, 0.041, 0.038 and 0.0085, consistent with the nominal-magnitude gap. Noise: the lab note states additive normal error, one SD for the whole experiment, equal for every peak, scaling between time points with the same factor that maps amounts onto intensities. That is the gain-scaled shape sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms, with one sigma_ctd_ms shared by name across all nine observables. Per-peak sigmas would rest on 4 points each and collapse toward zero on peaks the model fits exactly. data_signals is inconclusive (n = 1, no replicates), so this choice follows the lab note rather than a replicate test. The scale stays lin because this peak is zero once (log illegal) and the error is stated to be additive. An assumption that cannot be tested here: every phosphorylation count has the same ionisation and detection response. A count-dependent response factor would be confounded with the cooperativity parameter cp, so it is named rather than estimated. Evidence: direct (the lab note names the assay, the units and the error model)."

A position-resolved candidate maps this label to its all-marked configuration. Signals are relative per injection (units arbitrary; spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 over conserved substrate). So there is one scale factor per time point, shared by the nine peaks of the spectrum (group ctd_ms), and no offset because no background or blank is described. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed, unestimated 100 uM CTD total, not by pin_first_to_one. The peak is zero at 3 of 4 times, so log and pure proportional noise are illegal. The lab note states additive normal error with one experiment-wide SD for every peak, scaled by each spectrum's gain: sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with one shared sigma_ctd_ms. A sigma for this peak alone would be unidentifiable from one nonzero point. data_signals is inconclusive (n = 1). Equal ionisation across counts is assumed rather than estimated, since it is degenerate with cp. Evidence: direct (lab note)."

      "overrides": {
        "CTD_0": 100.0,
        "CTD_1": 0.0,
        "CTD_2": 0.0,
        "CTD_3": 0.0,
        "CTD_4": 0.0,
        "CTD_5": 0.0,
        "CTD_6": 0.0,
        "CTD_7": 0.0,
        "CTD_8": 0.0,
        "ATP": 3000.0,
        "ADP": 0.0,
        "PTEFb": 1.0
      },
      "preequilibration": false,
      "rationale": "The intent lists no perturbation. The data hold a single label: one purified in vitro P-TEFb kinase reaction, sampled at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min with no replicates. That makes exactly one condition, and none is invented. The overrides only restate the reaction mix as the lab note gives it (tier direct: the note states amounts and sampling times), so the audit can see what this condition was. These values match the model's initial values, so they change nothing in the simulation. CTD_0 = 100 uM, the recombinant 8-heptarepeat substrate, all unmodified at the start of the reaction. CTD_1..CTD_8 = 0 uM, since no modified substrate exists at t = 0. ATP = 3000 uM (3 mM at start, model unit uM, so there is no unit slip). ADP = 0 uM, as no phosphoryl transfer has occurred yet. PTEFb = 1 relative unit: the glossary says it is catalytic and constant, with its absolute concentration absorbed into kmod; the note gives no kinase concentration, so 1 is a convention, not a measured dose. No assignment rules or initial assignments exist, so these initial-value overrides are not silently ignored. The CTD_0 = 100 uM total is what pins the absolute scale in the observation draft. Its per-time-point gains (intensity per uM) are identified only because this total is fixed and unestimated. Estimating it would make it degenerate with the scale factors. Likewise, kmod absorbs kinase amount, so PTEFb must stay fixed. No parameter is overridden. kmod, cp and q_proc are mechanism parameters to be estimated or switched by model selection, not properties of this condition. The glossary marks none of them 'set per condition', which is expected for a single-condition design. K_ATP stays at its construction-fixed 50 uM. No population factor exists, so nothing is split per group. Pre-equilibration is false. t = 0 is the moment kinase, substrate and ATP are combined, not a settled baseline. basal_state confirms that the model's only steady state is full modification (CTD_8), so pre-equilibrating would run the reaction to completion before the first sample. Correction to design_summary: phos1_rel..phos8_rel were guessed as 'design' factors, but they are measurements (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), like phos0_rel. Their few unique values reflect only four rows with exact zeros, not factor levels. The 2916-cell 'factorial' is therefore spurious."
    }
  ]
}

residual sensitivities (AMICI, sigma residuals included) at the MLE, FIM = J^T J
flat combinations
0 beyond 8 decades

A SPECTRUM, not a rank. A direction many decades below the largest is a parameter combination the data barely constrain; a spectrum with no such direction proves nothing, because this is a local screen at one point. A model can be comprehensively non-identifiable and still predict well — the flat combinations and the prediction bands are two halves of one sentence, and neither blocks unless the intent says parameter values are the deliverable.

Structural flat directions, before the fit and at it

structural flat directions: none before the fit, none at it

A structural direction is flat at every parameter value, so it is flat near the nominal and around the optimum alike; one flat in only one of the two places is local, not structural. An indicator: AIC and BIC charge every estimated parameter. Method: the residual Jacobian at the MLE (the information screen's own) and at 2 random points within ±0.5 (scaled units) of it, each normalised, stacked; each pre-fit direction is tested along its own vector (the candidate's `structural_nulls_at_mle` record).

Diagnosis

full diagnosis

Within the five fitted candidates, M5_neighbour_and_count is selected decisively. Its AIC is -166.40, its Akaike weight 0.9971, and the indistinguishable set is {M5_neighbour_and_count}. The others trail by ΔAIC 11.90 (M3_neighbour), 17.12 (M2_count_coop), 18.50 (M4_processive) and 55.69 (M1_independent); petab_select agrees. OBSERVATION MODEL AS FITTED. Each of the 36 cells is y_n(t_j) = sc_ctd_ms_tj * [CTD with n phosphates](t_j) + e, with e ~ N(0, (sigma_ctd_ms * sc_ctd_ms_tj)^2), on a linear scale. Each spectrum has one free scale: t0 0.009986, t60 0.03971, t120 0.03844 and t960 0.008519 per µM. These map 100 µM to 1.00/3.97/3.84/0.85, against measured sums of 1.00/4.07/3.79/0.85. One sigma_ctd_ms = 1.012 µM-equivalent is shared by every cell. Check: the phos5 1-h residual of 0.1027 equals 2.555 x 1.012 x 0.03971. Substrate conservation holds to 1e-13. WHY M5 WINS (attribution). - Against M1, the 1-h spectrum pays: phos1 3.27, phos3 2.63, phos0 2.29 and phos2 1.71 in -log L. An independent, homogeneous model must give a binomial, but the measured 1-h distribution is much broader. Measured phos0 is 0.394 against 0.183 predicted, and the variance is about 1.5x binomial at the same mean. - Against M2 and M3, the gain is in phos2 at 1 h (2.77, 2.13), phos4 at 1 h (1.49, 1.38) and phos7 at 2 h (1.32, 1.76). M5 gives back phos0 at 1 h and phos2/phos6 at 2 h. - Against M4, the gain is phos7 at 16 h (3.21; M4's slower base rate leaves 3% stuck at seven), phos1 at 1 h (1.70) and phos8 at 2 h (1.62; M4 predicts 0.145 where 0 was measured). M4 is better on the 1-h upper tail (phos5 -2.66, phos6 -1.73). The data demand a distribution that is broad at 1 h, has an empty phos8 peak at 2 h, and is complete at 16 h. M5 gets there by pairing count acceleration (cp 1.588) with nb 0.314. If nb is a per-neighbour multiplicative factor with neutral value 1, like cp, this brakes the filling of flanked gaps late in the reaction. TWO LIMITS ON THIS RESULT. (i) Roughly half of every margin is sigma bookkeeping, not mechanism. The 18 cells at 0 h and 16 h are fitted to within noise by every model (19 measured values are exact zeros). Each adds log(sigma_rival/sigma_M5) to the winner: 0.193 per cell against M3, about 3.5 of its 6.95 Δ(-log L). On the 18 informative cells at 1 h and 2 h, the margin over M3 is about ΔAIC 5. That is still above 2, but the weight is nearer 0.9 than 0.997. Exact zeros are also not what the stated additive Gaussian noise produces. (ii) The neighbour term is seen only through the count distribution, and its value moves across neutral between models (nb 1.812 in M3, 0.314 in M5). What it buys in M5 is a step-rate profile that rises through mid-counts and brakes at the end, which M2's single cp cannot express. No count-only candidate with an equally flexible step-rate profile was fitted. So this round does not show that the effect is specifically about immediate neighbours. REMAINING STRUCTURE. The per-series shape tools are degenerate here: each peak x time is its own observable with n = 1, so sign runs, autocorrelation and residual_forms carry no shape. Read across counts within each spectrum, M5's largest residuals form one pattern: - the 1-h upper tail is underpredicted (phos5 +2.6 sigma, 0.352 vs 0.250; phos6 +2.0 sigma); - the 2-h top is overpredicted (phos8 -2.3 sigma, 0 vs 0.088; phos7 -2.0 sigma); - the 2-h low tail is heavier than any candidate gives (phos1 at 2 h is 0.191, against at most 0.164). There are no replicates, sigma is fitted from these same residuals, and the noise check has n = 1 per cell. Absolute adequacy therefore cannot be judged; chi2/dof is about 1 by construction. IDENTIFIABILITY. The FIM spans 2.86 decades with no flat direction; its smallest eigenvector is sigma_ctd_ms. Profiles were not computed, so no intervals exist. The nested reductions still exceed the 1.92 profile threshold even if halved: M2 drops nb (Δ(-log L) 9.56) and M3 fixes cp = 1 (6.95). Both terms are therefore non-null within M5. ANSWERS TO THE INTENT. - 'The rate depends on nothing at all' is rejected for a homogeneous substrate. Static substrate heterogeneity was not tried. - Count-only and neighbour-only each fall short of both together. Whether the second term is specifically an immediate-neighbour effect is not established. - Distributive vs processive: processivity alone (q_proc 0.2124) loses by ΔAIC 18.5, which is consistent with the by-eye call. But processivity was never combined with the coupling terms, and M4 fits the 1-h upper tail best. 'Distributive' therefore holds only against processivity alone. - Global effects cannot produce the non-binomial shape. These are ATP (3 mM with at most 0.8 mM consumed, K_ATP fixed at 50), kinase loss and product inhibition. They multiply every step equally and only re-time the trajectory. REVISE, with one move: fit a count-only candidate with a three-parameter step-rate profile and compare its -log L with M5's -91.20.

Misfit hypotheses

  • 1 (highest). The per-step rate profile is still wrong at the top of the distribution. …
  • 2. The distribution broadens from the slow side, not by accelerating leaders. …
  • 3. A processive component on top of the coupling terms. M4 is the best candidate on phos4/phos5/phos6 at 1 h (rmse 0.021/0.042/0.021 vs M5's …
all 4 hypotheses, in full
  • 1 (highest). The per-step rate profile is still wrong at the top of the distribution. M5 is too slow into the upper counts at 1 h: phos5 +2.6 sigma (0.352 vs 0.250) and phos6 +2.0 sigma (0.158 vs 0.076). It is too fast into them at 2 h: phos8 -2.3 sigma (measured 0 vs 0.088) and phos7 -2.0 sigma (0.195 vs 0.273). Every coupled or processive candidate predicts 0.088-0.145 for phos8 at 2 h; only M1 (0.021) does not. Yet completion by 16 h needs a final step faster than M4's base rate of 0.0052/min. This points at a step rate that rises through mid-counts and drops for the last one or two repeats. That could be a non-monotone count dependence, or one intrinsically slow repeat such as a construct-terminal one. cp-type acceleration plus nb only approximates it. A count-only candidate with a separate final-step factor would test it.
  • 2. The distribution broadens from the slow side, not by accelerating leaders. The 2-h low tail is heavier than every candidate gives: phos1 at 2 h is 0.191 measured vs 0.076-0.164 predicted, phos0 0.061 vs at most 0.051, and phos2 is +1.5 sigma under M5. Meanwhile the top end is empty. A slower substrate sub-population with independent sites broadens the distribution without populating phos7-phos8. That would be an alternative to cooperativity and would reopen 'the rate depends on nothing at all'. It needs two parameters (fraction and rate ratio) and is not in the candidate set.
  • 3. A processive component on top of the coupling terms. M4 is the best candidate on phos4/phos5/phos6 at 1 h (rmse 0.021/0.042/0.021 vs M5's 0.048/0.103/0.082). It fails mainly at the end: 0.145 for phos8 at 2 h, and 3% left at phos7 at 16 h. M5 with q_proc free was never fitted.
  • 4 (lowest). Observation layer. Equal MS response for every phospho-state is assumed and cannot be tested here. A monotone trend in response with phosphate number cannot both raise phos5-6 at 1 h and lower phos7-8 at 2 h, so it does not explain the main pattern. The 19 exact zeros behave as non-detections rather than Gaussian measurements. The phos8 zero at 2 h is not a detection artefact, though: phos0 at 2 h (0.061) was reported, which is below phos8's predicted 0.088. The zeros' main effect is on the size of the AIC margins, not on which model is selected.

decisions_md (round decision record, assembled by the engine from the agents' structured records)
# Decision record — round_0

## Model construction (agent)

- **The base tracks how many of the 8 repeats each molecule carries (CTD_0..CTD_8), not which. It is the exact count lumping of the 256-configuration positional model whenever the per-repeat rate does not depend on the state of the immediate neighbours. The positional (neighbour) model is not written in this reply.** **[asked the user]**
  - why: For every rate rule this base can switch on (independent repeats, count cooperativity cp^n, processive continuation that picks among the remaining unmodified repeats), all unmodified repeats of a molecule with n marks share one rate, so the 256 configurations are strongly lumpable by n and these 9 states reproduce the positional model's count distribution exactly. The 'nothing at all', 'cooperativity' and 'distributive vs processive' hypotheses therefore lose nothing by being counted. A nearest-neighbour effect is the one hypothesis that breaks the lumping, so it cannot be a switch on this base. Two previous replies to this brief failed the contract outright; a 1024-reaction hand enumeration, together with its 256-entry glossary and network, is not something this reply can carry reliably or check without execution. The next decision gives the exact rule so the positional model can be generated mechanically. A generator check comes free: at nb = 1 it must reproduce this base trajectory for trajectory.
  - alternatives: Full 256-configuration model written out by hand as the base (the user's stated preference; not deliverable reliably here). Mirror-symmetry reduction to 136 orbits (exact, but still ~500 reactions with multiplicities and harder to audit). Pair or domain-count approximations (n, number of marked runs) were rejected because they are not exact, and the lab note asks that the question not be settled from counts alone.
  - source: lab_note ['Any model that simulates is acceptable, whether it tracks only how many repeats are modified or which repeats are modified (with eight repeats, 256 configurations).'] (user-provided) — a count-resolved model is an admissible description
  - source: lab_note ['If a possibility can only be represented by tracking which repeats are modified, we would rather see that model fitted than the question settled by argument from the counts alone.'] (user-provided) — the neighbour hypothesis must be fitted as a positional model, not argued away
  - source: general_knowledge [] (assumed) — strong lumpability of a Markov chain: states may be aggregated exactly when every state in a block has the same total rate into each other block
  - evidence tier: default · confidence: medium
- **Exact construction rule for the positional (neighbour) candidate, to be generated and not hand-written. Species C_b1b2b3b4b5b6b7b8 (b_i = 1 if repeat i, numbered from the N-terminus, is phosphorylated), C_00000000 = 100 uM, all others 0. For every configuration and every unmodified repeat i, one reaction to the configuration with b_i = 1, consuming one ATP and producing one ADP. Rate: vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^n*nb^m*C, where n = marks on the molecule and m = marked immediate neighbours of i (0 to 2; repeats 1 and 8 have one neighbour). New parameter nb, a fold change per marked neighbour: nominal and neutral value 1, bounds 0.01 to 100.**
  - why: This is the minimal positional extension that separates 'a mark changes its neighbours' rate' (nb) from 'the rate depends on how many marks the molecule carries' (cp) and from neither (nb = cp = 1). It is 8*2^7 = 1024 reactions. Summing C over the C(8,n) configurations with n marks gives CTD_n, so readouts map onto it exactly as onto this base. nb < 1 (neighbour inhibition) jams molecules near 3 to 4 non-adjacent marks before slow filling, and that stall at intermediate counts between 2 h and 16 h is something cp alone cannot shape. nb > 1 gives nucleation-and-growth (bimodal 0-versus-high counts at 1 to 2 h), which cp > 1 and processivity also give. That is the likely indistinguishable set.
  - alternatives: A directional neighbour effect (separate factors for N- and C-side neighbours) was not chosen: counts carry no positional information to separate the two directions, so it would add a flat direction. Pairwise or longer-range interactions were not chosen either: they are not the hypothesis named.
  - source: lab_note ['that the modification of one repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, as opposed to the rate depending only on how many repeats of the molecule are already modified (cooperativity between repeats ...), or on nothing at all'] (user-provided) — the three hypotheses to compare, with neighbours meaning immediate neighbours
  - source: lab_note ['It does not resolve which repeats those are.'] (user-provided) — only counts are observed, so the positional model is observed through sums over configurations
  - source: lab_note ['The simulator reserves the single letters x, k, p, y, w, h and t'] (user-provided) — naming: C_..., nb, cp avoid the reserved letters
  - evidence tier: to_be_estimated · confidence: medium
- **Distributive single-repeat steps J0..J7. Each unmodified repeat is modified at kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP), mass action in the substrate at constant enzyme, so a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n) times that rate. The template is phosphorylation X -> X_p with the kinase as modifier. Irreversible: no reverse step and no phosphatase.**
  - why: The assay is purified kinase, CTD and ATP with no phosphatase, so removal of phosphate is not modelled. The kinase is catalytic and constant, so its level enters as a fixed multiplier. Mass action in CTD assumes the kinase is far from saturated by substrate. Neither the enzyme concentration nor a CTD Km is given, so saturation cannot be decided from the note. If all unmodified repeats bind alike, saturation would only reparameterise time by a factor common to every reaction (the same sequence of distributions, a different clock). With three post-zero time points that clock change is largely absorbed by kmod and cp, so it is named unresolved rather than built in. With cp = 1 and q_proc = 0 the count distribution is binomial(8, 1 - exp(-r*t)): the independent-repeat ('nothing at all') hypothesis.
  - alternatives: Michaelis-Menten in CTD with competition among all substrate forms (left out: time warp only, not identifiable here). Reversible steps (no phosphatase present).
  - source: lab_note ['There is no transcription, no DNA, no polymerase — only a purified CTD substrate, purified kinase, and ATP in buffer.'] (user-provided) — no phosphatase, no other reactions
  - source: lab_note ['Kinase: P-TEFb, catalytic. It is not consumed and its concentration does not change over the experiment.'] (user-provided) — enzyme enters as a constant modifier
  - source: general_knowledge [] (assumed) — mass action at constant enzyme is the low-saturation limit of Michaelis-Menten kinetics
  - evidence tier: default · confidence: medium
- **Count-cooperativity switch cp: the per-repeat rate of a molecule carrying n marks is multiplied by cp^n. cp = 1 (base) turns it off; cp > 1 is positive and cp < 1 negative cooperativity between repeats.**
  - why: One parameter expresses 'the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified' as a constant fold change per existing mark, the additive free-energy form. It is the most parsimonious count-dependent law the data can constrain with 9 peaks at 3 informative time points. A free factor per n (7 parameters) would not be identifiable. Bounds 0.2 to 5 are 1.4 decades on cp but compound to ~10 decades on the n = 7 step. Wider bounds put the solver in stiff corners without adding plausible behaviour.
  - alternatives: A free rate per count n (unidentifiable). A saturating dependence on n (an extra shape parameter the data cannot see).
  - source: lab_note ['the rate depending only on how many repeats of the molecule are already modified (cooperativity between repeats, which was also raised as a possibility to look at)'] (user-provided) — count-dependent rate is one of the hypotheses to test
  - evidence tier: to_be_estimated · confidence: medium
- **Processivity switch q_proc on reactions Jp<n>_<j>. A binding event on a molecule with n marks starts at the same encounter rate as a distributive step. The encounter-level jump n -> n+j with geometric run length is the standard count-level representation, and its weights sum to 1, so q_proc changes what an encounter does, not how often encounters happen. Strong processivity predicts early bimodality (CTD_0 plus high counts, depleted intermediates at 1 h). Its difference from cp > 1 is memory: under processivity a released molecule returns to the slow distributive pace, so long-lived intermediates persist to the 16 h point. Sliding processivity (running along to the next repeat, stopped by an already-modified repeat) depends on positions and only exists in the positional model. It is not exactly lumpable and is likely aliased with nb > 1.

- **Five candidates. M1 is the base: independent repeats, strictly distributive. M2 switches on count cooperativity (cp estimated). M3 adds the nearest-neighbour effect (positional patch, nb estimated). M4 switches on processivity (q_proc estimated). M5 combines the neighbour effect with count cooperativity (nb and cp estimated) and says so.**

M1 is the 'nothing at all' and distributive reference that every 'required' verdict is measured against. M2, M3 and M4 each switch on exactly one feature. M5 is the model that contains M2 and M3 as nested cases, so the comparisons 'neighbour effect beyond count cooperativity' and the converse are direct, and the joint nb-cp profile is where the separability question is answered. Every switch acts on its own: cp, nb and q_proc each change the dynamics with the others at their neutral values. No candidate differs from another only in an inert switch.

- **The neighbour effect, which the base cannot express, is added as a patch in M3 and M5. The patch implements construction's positional rule exactly: rate per unmodified repeat = kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^n*nb^m, with m the number of marked immediate neighbours. It is written out state by state and reaction by reaction on 74 gap-structure classes and 257 reactions. These are the exact lumping of the 256-configuration, 1024-reaction model.**
  - why: An unmodified repeat's rate depends only on n and on whether its two neighbours are marked. That is fixed by its position inside the maximal stretch of unmarked repeats (gap) that contains it, and by the gap's type: interior (marks on both sides), end (chain terminus on one side), or the whole unmodified chain. Modifying a repeat changes only its own gap: it splits the gap into at most two gaps of determined types, or shrinks it by one. The multiset of gap lengths with their types is therefore a sufficient state. The lengths of marked runs, the order of interior gaps and the orientation of the chain do not enter any rate; the rule treats both termini alike. Configurations sharing a gap structure have identical exit rates to every target class, so the 256 configurations are strongly lumpable onto the 74 classes. The classes with n marks sum to the count distribution exactly, at every nb and cp. Built-in check: at nb = 1 every class with n marks has total exit coefficient 8 - n (for example G01_22: 5*nb), so M3 reproduces M1 and M5 reproduces M2 trajectory for trajectory. Writing the reduced network by hand carries far less risk of an enumeration error than 1024 hand-written lines.
  - alternatives: The literal 256-species, 1024-reaction enumeration. The note prefers the positional model written out rather than avoided, and it is written out here. The enumeration would only split each class into configurations with identical trajectories, so it gives the same likelihood and the same verdicts; it is not a different model. A positional readout (which repeats are marked) would need it, and none exists.

  - source: general_knowledge [strong lumpability of Markov chains (Kemeny-Snell); exact lumping of linear ODE networks by symmetry of the rate rule] (inferred) — class-level reactions reproduce the configuration-level count distribution exactly
  - source: lab_note [base_model decision: exact construction rule for the positional (neighbour) candidate] (inferred) — rate cp^n*nb^m, nb neutral 1, bounds 0.01 to 100
  - evidence tier: direct · confidence: high

Every flux into or out of a class with n marks moves CTD_n by the same amount, and CTD_n(0) equals its class sum, so CTD_n equals the sum of its classes identically. That identity now holds by stoichiometry, not by matching summed coefficients, so an error in any one coefficient cannot break it. A linear multistep integrator preserves the linear invariant to solver precision. The class reactions are the base's distributive single-repeat steps resolved by position, so J0 to J7 at zero rate are superseded, not contradicted. The base's processive Jp* reactions likewise sit at exactly zero rate in M3 and M5, where q_proc stays 0 and processivity is not composed with the positional model. The class rate laws read only the class amount, so listing CTD_n as a reactant changes no rate. The deliberate simplification is a second conservation class (sum over G = 100 uM) alongside sum over CTD_n = 100 uM. Both are intended and neither carries a free parameter.

Assignment rules CTD_n := sum of G_n were also rejected. They would require removing CTD_n from all 36 base reactions, which the patch grammar does not allow.

The data hold a single label: one purified in vitro P-TEFb kinase reaction, sampled at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min with no replicates. That makes exactly one condition, and none is invented. The overrides only restate the reaction mix as the lab note gives it (tier direct: the note states amounts and sampling times), so the audit can see what this condition was. These values match the model's initial values, so they change nothing in the simulation. CTD_0 = 100 uM, the recombinant 8-heptarepeat substrate, all unmodified at the start of the reaction. CTD_1..CTD_8 = 0 uM, since no modified substrate exists at t = 0. ATP = 3000 uM (3 mM at start, model unit uM, so there is no unit slip). ADP = 0 uM, as no phosphoryl transfer has occurred yet. PTEFb = 1 relative unit: the glossary says it is catalytic and constant, with its absolute concentration absorbed into kmod; the note gives no kinase concentration, so 1 is a convention, not a measured dose. No assignment rules or initial assignments exist, so these initial-value overrides are not silently ignored. The CTD_0 = 100 uM total is what pins the absolute scale in the observation draft. Its per-time-point gains (intensity per uM) are identified only because this total is fixed and unestimated. Estimating it would make it degenerate with the scale factors. Likewise, kmod absorbs kinase amount, so PTEFb must stay fixed. No parameter is overridden. kmod, cp and q_proc are mechanism parameters to be estimated or switched by model selection, not properties of this condition. The glossary marks none of them 'set per condition', which is expected for a single-condition design. K_ATP stays at its construction-fixed 50 uM. No population factor exists, so nothing is split per group. Pre-equilibration is false. t = 0 is the moment kinase, substrate and ATP are combined, not a settled baseline. basal_state confirms that the model's only steady state is full modification (CTD_8), so pre-equilibrating would run the reaction to completion before the first sample. Correction to design_summary: phos1_rel..phos8_rel were guessed as 'design' factors, but they are measurements (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), like phos0_rel. Their few unique values reflect only four rows with exact zeros, not factor levels. The 2916-cell 'factorial' is therefore spurious.

## Independent construction audit (fresh context, artifacts only)

- CONCERN — citation honesty: No external literature is cited and no entry is marked resolution: unresolvable. The general-knowledge statements are accurate: strong lumpability (Kemeny-Snell), mass action as the low-saturation limit of Michaelis-Menten, and protein-kinase ATP Km of 10-100 uM. Several entries are mis-sourced, though. (1) Decision 10 (five candidates) evidence 2, decision 11 (positional patch) evidence 3 and decision 14 (indistinguishable set) evidence 2 give source 'lab_note', but their locators ('base_model decisions (count cooperativity, processivity switches)', 'base_model decision: exact construction rule...', 'base_model decision: not in the base...') are the build report's own decisions 2, 4, 5 and 8; the lab note contains no such text. (2) Decisions 12, 13 and 15 file engine error logs ('previous_attempt_errors', 'attempt_history'), domain-pack entries and human feedback (petablint rejection) under source 'general_knowledge'. The origins ('inferred', 'user-provided') show nothing is invented, but the source fields should name the build report, the engine log, the pack and the human feedback so a reader can check them.
- OK — support: Each lab-note quote matches its decision. Purified components only supports no phosphatase and irreversibility (decision 3). Catalytic and constant kinase supports PTEFb as a fixed modifier (decision 7). 3 mM ATP with 100 uM x 8 repeats supports the at-most-800 uM consumption argument and K_ATP being immaterial (decision 6). One bit per repeat supports the 9 count states. The relative, drifting intensities support per-time-point scales in the observation layer (decision 9). The three-hypothesis passage supports cp, nb and the five-candidate design. The general-knowledge entries back only modelling-form choices (lumpability, the mass-action limit, the continuation-probability representation of processivity) and are recorded as assumed or inferred. No correlational or adjacent material is recorded as mechanism.
- CONCERN — rationale quality: Most rationales argue from the system: ATP stays saturating (factor about 0.98); 0.2-5 on cp compounds to about 10 decades at n = 7; neighbour inhibition jams at 3-4 non-adjacent marks; processivity's memory distinguishes it from cp > 1. Three specific problems. (a) Decision 13 says that with cp^7 'the fastest corner reaches rates about 1e4-fold above the per-repeat kmod'. In M5 at cp = 5, nb = 100, Q_G00_1_G00 carries cp^7*nb^2 = 78125*1e4, about 7.8e8. The slow corner (cp = 0.2, nb = 0.01) is about 1.3e-9, so the box spans about 18 decades on that step, not 8. The 1e4 holds only for M3 (cp = 1). The corner-integrability check the decision asks for should use the correct span. (b) Decisions 1 and 2 are stale relative to decision 11. Decision 1 says 'The positional (neighbour) model is not written in this reply' and still carries user_decision_required: true with options A (generate 1024 reactions mechanically) and B (hand-enumerate 256 states). What was delivered is neither: a hand-written exact 74-class lumping. The human at the scope gate is asked a question that no longer describes the record. Part of decision 1's rationale is also about the builder's capacity ('Two previous replies ... failed the contract') rather than the system. (c) Decision 11 says the full enumeration 'would only split each class into configurations with identical trajectories'. That is false for nb != 1. For example, 10110000 and 11010000 are both in G04_1 but receive different inflows: 10110000 gets nb from 10100000, nb from 10010000 and 1 from 00110000; 11010000 gets 1 from 11000000, nb from 10010000 and nb from 01010000. Only the class sums are exact. The conclusion (same likelihood and verdicts) still holds.
- OK — tier honesty: The default labels are appropriate: decision 3 (mass action in CTD, irreversibility), decision 6 (K_ATP fixed at 50 uM from a generic range, argued immaterial because ATP >> K_ATP throughout), decision 1 (count-level base) and decision 13 (bounds). cp, nb and q_proc are correctly to_be_estimated. 'direct' on decision 7 (CTD_0(0) = 100 uM, constant kinase), decision 9 (per-time-point scaling) and the J0-J7 stoichiometry rests on lab-note statements. 'direct'/high on decisions 11, 12 and 15 is generous: they rest on a lumping derivation and engine workarounds, not system evidence. The lumping was verified under structure sanity, so no mechanistic support is overstated. Nothing labelled default has unclaimed support.
- OK — structure sanity: The base Antimony matches the network: 12 species, and J0-J7 plus 28 Jp reactions (36 in total) with j ATP consumed per j-repeat run. The per-repeat encounter rate is (8-n)*cp^n. Run weights are q^(j-1)(1-q), with q^(r-1) for the run that completes the molecule, so J7 correctly lacks (1-q_proc) and Jp6_2 = q_proc; each encounter's weights sum to 1. The M3/M5 patch was checked class by class against decision 2's rule. The 74 gap classes are exactly the gap structures with n = 0..8 marks (1, 4, 16, 20, 16, 9, 5, 2, 1), and the 257 reactions have the correct target classes. nb exponents equal the number of marked immediate neighbours, including terminal repeats, and cp powers equal n. Each class's coefficients sum to 8-n at nb = 1 (for example G04_1: nb^2+nb+3; G01_22: 5nb; G00_111: 3nb^2). Each Q reaction also moves CTD_n to CTD_n+1 and consumes one ATP, so CTD_n equals its class sum identically. J0-J7 at zero rate and the Jp reactions at q_proc = 0 contribute nothing in M3/M5. Minor gap: kmod's nominal value (0.01 per min) and its estimation scale and bounds are not recorded in any decision.
- CONCERN — candidate set: The reference model M1 (cp = 1, q_proc = 0, no positional term) is present, as both the three-way test and the distributive test need. M2 (cp), M3 (nb, cp held at 1) and M4 (q_proc) each switch on one feature. M5 declares its nb+cp combination and carries the identical positional patch, which reduces to M2 at nb = 1 and to M3 at cp = 1. The J0-J7 zeroing and Q-reaction bookkeeping change no trajectory at neutral values, and kmod and K_ATP are handled identically across all five, so no candidate differs outside its named feature. The concern is M4. It implements random-site continuation: the kinase picks any remaining unmodified repeat. The lab note defines processive as 'holding on and running along the substrate', and asks that possibilities representable only positionally be fitted rather than settled from counts. Sliding processivity was set aside in decisions 5, 10 and 14 as 'likely aliased with nb > 1' to stay within five candidates, which is an argument from counts. M4's decision rule ('If it reaches the lower bound ... distributive action is supported') therefore overstates. A q_proc at its lower bound would exclude only random-site processivity. Either the M4 verdict should be reported as testing random-site processivity only, with sliding listed as untested, or the human should decide whether a positional sliding candidate replaces M5 or goes beyond the cap.

## Independent checker (fresh context, artifacts only)

- OK — noise model vs readout technique: Checked against the lab note's stated error model for the intact-mass MS readout. Every observable uses a normal distribution on a lin scale. Its noise SD is observableParameter1 × noiseParameter1, which is the per-spectrum factor times the single sigma_ctd_ms. This matches the note's claims: additive Gaussian error, one SD for all peaks, scaled by the same factor that maps amounts to intensities at that time point. Reusing observableParameter1 in noiseFormula guarantees the noise and signal factors are the same parameter. The lin scale tolerates the 19 exact zeros, where a log transform would fail. No error column exists, so there is no SD/SEM question, and estimating sigma is the only option. Doubt only: MS peak noise often grows with intensity. The assembly follows the note's additive claim, which is defensible, but residuals at 60 and 120 min should be checked for intensity dependence.
- CONCERN — structurally exact likelihood terms under the shared estimated sigma: Checked the t=0 and t=960 rows against the initial-condition encoding and the per-time-point scales. At t=0 every candidate mechanism reproduces all nine terms with zero residual by construction. CTD_1..CTD_8 start at exactly 0, matching the exact-zero data. The free sc_ctd_ms_t0 (best value about 0.01, inside its box) absorbs the single nonzero peak. At t=960 the free sc_ctd_ms_t960 likewise absorbs phos8. These terms carry no information about mechanism, but they still count in the likelihood and pull the shared sigma_ctd_ms estimate toward zero. With sigma estimated, likelihood differences between candidates scale with the total number of terms. That inflates the evidence separating mechanisms, which affects the Akaike weights the intent requires to be reported honestly, as well as profile-based intervals. The data flags asked the observation model to account for the exact zeros. Nothing in observables or parameters shows that this was considered. Point estimates of kmod, cp and q_proc are not affected; sigma and the model-selection evidence are.
- OK — condition encoding vs experiment description: Reconstructed the single treatment from its overrides alone: 100 µM CTD, all in CTD_0; ATP 3000 µM (3 mM); ADP 0; PTEFb 1. This matches the note's 8-repeat substrate at 100 µM, 3 mM ATP, a catalytic kinase that is never consumed, and t=0 data with all signal in phos0. One condition matches the note's one in vitro treatment sampled over time. No pre-equilibration is used, which is correct: there is no pre-treatment, and the reaction starts at mixing. Fixing PTEFb at 1 is consistent with the glossary's statement that kinase concentration is absorbed into kmod. Fixed K_ATP of 50 µM is harmless, since at most 800 µM ATP is consumed out of 3000.
- OK — scaling and offset vs declared units: Checked against the note's statement that intensities are arbitrary, drift between injections and are not comparable across time points. There are four per-time-point scale factors (t0, t60, t120, t960). This is per-spectrum scaling with an explicit stated reason, not unexplained per-condition scaling. No information is lost that the data ever held, because cross-time amounts are declared incomparable, and each time point keeps its within-spectrum shape. The factors are identifiable rather than flat: the model total is fixed and conserved at 100 µM, so each factor is pinned near row-sum/100 (about 0.0085 to 0.041), well inside the 1e-3 to 1e3 log10 box. There is no offset, which is appropriate: the note gives no background story, and the exact-zero empty peaks argue against one. Consequence to carry into the report: each informative spectrum (60, 120 min) gives up one degree of freedom to its factor.
- OK — observable mapping vs what the assay measures: Checked each mapping against the glossary lumps and the intact-mass readout. Each phosN observable maps to CTD_n, which lumps all C(8,n) configurations with n marks. That is exactly what one mass peak sees, since position is not resolved and the one-bit-per-repeat convention makes count equal phosphate number. No lumped state is omitted. ATP, ADP and PTEFb are correctly left unobserved, and no kinase-bound substrate species exists that would need adding to a total. I cannot verify from these artifacts that each measurement row uses the observable id matching its own time point; the ids hard-wire the time point. Doubt: the mapping assumes every phospho-form ionises with the same response factor within a spectrum, as the note's model also does. A count-dependent response would tilt peak heights systematically with n, in a way the count-cooperativity factor cp could absorb. This is a confound for the cooperativity conclusion that should be named in the report, not a fault in the table.
- CONCERN — hypothesis space vs the mechanistic question asked: Checked the glossary species and the parameters table against the intent and the lab note. The note asks that neighbour-dependent modification be fitted rather than settled by argument, explicitly inviting the 256-configuration model. The assembly holds only count-indexed species CTD_0..CTD_8, plus switches for count cooperativity (cp) and processivity (q_proc). A rate that depends on whether a repeat's immediate neighbours are modified is not a function of CTD_n alone, so it cannot be expressed in this state space. No parameter for it exists. As assembled, the comparison covers only two of the three hypotheses the intent names, and Akaike weights would be computed over a set that omits the hypothesis the note most wants tested. Minor, related: q_proc's distributive null value of 0 lies outside its own log10 box (1e-4 to 0.99) and has no finite log10 value. The base model's fixed 0 on a log10 scale may need checking in the tooling, and the switched-on test compares against q_proc ≥ 1e-4 rather than exactly distributive.
